# Brief 08: Organisation redesign

Audience: Tidewater Insurance executive committee.
Decision: approve a move from seven to five management layers and a hybrid claims structure.
Format: 9 slides, density balanced. Start with a cover and end with next steps.
Data: data.csv holds layers and spans by business unit used on slides 3 and 4.

## Facts

F1: Tidewater employs 3,150 people; there are 612 managers and 7 management layers from CEO to front line.
F2: The average span of control is 4.2 direct reports; the target is 8.
F3: Layers and average span by unit: Claims 7 layers and span 3.8; Underwriting 6 and 4.6; Distribution 7 and 4.1; Corporate 6 and 4.5.
F4: Eleven functions are duplicated across four regional units, including claims support, finance and HR.
F5: Large claims above $50k take 21 days to decide; peers take 14.
F6: Only 58% of employees favourable on decision speed in the last survey.
F7: Manager headcount bridge: 612 today, -150 span consolidation, -52 duplicated functions, -30 natural attrition, 380 target.
F8: Annual savings are $17M, with one-time cost of $11M.
F9: Options scored 0-4: keep regional units, functional model, hybrid (recommended): functional claims and underwriting, regional distribution.
F10: Rollout: design in Q1, layers removed in Q2 and Q3, new structure complete by Q4 2027.
F11: Risk: 24 critical roles hold knowledge of large claims; a retention plan is needed before announcements.
